kept.q: A school librarian wants to arrange 4 different Mathematics textbooks in a row on a shelf. In how many ways can this be done?
kept.explanation: Since all 4 books are different and order matters, the number of arrangements is 4! = 4x3x2x1 = 24.
kept.pidgin: Since all di 4 books different and arrangement matter, na 4! we go use = 4x3x2x1 = 24.

kept.q: A school football club has 6 boys and 5 girls. A mixed team of 4 is to be chosen to represent the club such that exactly 2 boys and 2 girls are selected. In how many ways can this team be formed?
kept.explanation: Choose 2 boys from 6: C(6,2)=15. Choose 2 girls from 5: C(5,2)=10. Multiply the two results: 15 x 10 = 150.
kept.pidgin: Pick 2 boys from 6: C(6,2)=15. Pick 2 girls from 5: C(5,2)=10. Multiply dem: 15 x 10 = 150.

kept.q: Find the number of distinct ways the letters of the word ABUJA can be arranged.
kept.explanation: ABUJA has 5 letters with the letter A repeated twice. The number of distinct arrangements is 5!/2! = 120/2 = 60.
kept.pidgin: ABUJA get 5 letters, but letter A dey repeat two times. Di distinct arrangements na 5!/2! = 120/2 = 60.

kept.q: A school is to send a delegation of 5 students out of 8 students to a competition. Among the 8 students are Chidi and Ngozi, who are known rivals and must not both be chosen together in the same delegation. How many valid delegations can be formed?
kept.explanation: Total ways to choose any 5 from 8 is C(8,5)=56. Ways where both Chidi and Ngozi are included: choose the remaining 3 from the other 6 students, C(6,3)=20. Subtract the unwanted cases: 56-20=36.
kept.pidgin: Total ways to pick 5 from 8 na C(8,5)=56. Di ways wey Chidi and Ngozi go dey together na C(6,3)=20 (pick remaining 3 from di other 6). So we remove di bad ones: 56-20=36.
